books.section: Topic 4.13 The Society of the South in the Early Republic, A. Slavery and the Southern “Way of Life”

primary_sources: Alexis de Tocqueville, Democracy in America, 1835

stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.13 A: The South grew distinct from the rest of the country. Slavery and cotton came to define Southern society, and white Southerners defended slavery as part of their way of life. Some defenders compared Northern factory workers, who could be fired when business was slow, with enslaved people, who were fed and housed by their owners. Alexis de Tocqueville, visiting in the 1830s, wrote that slavery was the main source of the South's distinctiveness.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.13 A (Southern defense of slavery; Tocqueville on slavery as the main source of Southern distinctiveness).

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.13 A
stem: Tocqueville wrote that slavery was the main source of the South's distinctiveness. What did he mean?

options.text: Only the South had farms, while the North had none at all
options.misconception: The North had farms too; farming was not what made the South distinct.

options.text: Slavery shaped the South's culture, politics, and identity
The South had abolished slavery while the North kept it
options.misconception: The reverse is true: the North abolished slavery while the South kept it.

options.text: Slavery mattered little to Southern life by the 1830s
options.misconception: Slavery mattered more by the 1830s, as cotton and the defense of slavery grew.

rationales.A: The North had farms too. Farming was not what made the South distinct.
rationales.B: Slavery set the South's labor, its politics, its manners, and its pride apart from the North, so it was the main source of the region's distinctiveness.
rationales.C: The reverse is true: the North abolished slavery while the South kept it.
rationales.D: Slavery mattered more by the 1830s, as cotton and the defense of slavery grew.
rationales.general:
1. Read Tocqueville's claim. Slavery was the main source of what made the South different.
2. Ask what slavery touches. It sets the labor system, the politics, and the daily manners of a place.
3. Name the meaning. No other single thing shaped Southern culture, politics, and identity as much.
Background: Black people made up a large share of the South's population, a share no Northern state matched.
Remember: when one fact explains a whole region, it is usually the one that touches daily life.
